criteria.rationale: Verified: the normal Linux CLI enables the isolated shim; its subtree is the adapter run, it reaps children, and the focused regression tests passed. The live-owner release check passed, and release records failed status with a receipt. Unresolved: non-Linux Unix waiting and non-Linux PID reporting (N2/N3), the Linux scan bound (N4), and release recovery across a partial witness publication (N5). Accepted residuals in spec L1/L3/L4/L6 remain explicit; L6 is N1. The Windows descendant test was not executable on this Linux host.
The exclusive release lock and live-owner refusal tests pass, but the non-Linux Unix path does not wait for process-group exit; the Linux per-entry scan can also exceed the stated bound (N4).
The cancel option is additive, the run and receipt remain schema version 1, and the entrypoint stays in the existing delegate CLI contract. The delegated-surface integration evidence is sealed.
Attempt ID validation, marker/liveness checks, confirmation for markerless reservations, bounded directory reads, and error returns are covered by the unit suite; focused release tests passed.
The change touches local review dispatch and delegation storage, not an external service contract. The integration assessment's three unobserved HTTP consumers are unrelated to these changed paths.
Linux records reaped PIDs, but the Windows job and non-Linux Unix paths do not populate the ended-process list in safety.limitations.
Released attempts retain ordinary v1 failed-run and receipt records; older record readers keep their existing fields and meaning. The confirm-abandoned CLI flag is additive.

The normal interrupted-dispatch retry path passes, but a release interrupted between run-witness publication and run-record publication leaves history incomplete and the attempt unrecoverable; N2 and N4 also leave R1 gaps.

D1 addresses escaped-session descendants while isolating subreaper authority in a shim, avoiding the process-wide adoption risk. D2 closes an abandoned reservation with the same failed-run and receipt records old readers consume. The sealed design assessment reports no structural deltas; the remaining issues are implementation coverage gaps.

The brief uses review-brief/10 and asks commands to finish. English and pt-BR manuals and scaffold copies describe Linux shim, the no-shim fallback, other Unix process groups, Windows jobs, and abandoned-attempt release.
delegate ls names stalled causes and the release command; cancel reports the released run and status, and refusal paths give the missing liveness or operator-confirmation condition.

R3/R4 and the ordinary R5/R6 retry paths have relevant tests, but R1's bounded wait still has platform/scan gaps (N2/N4), R2 lacks ended-PID records outside Linux (N3), and interrupted release publication can still strand R5/R6 (N5).
The implementation, CLI, brief, manuals, and generated scaffold copies stay within the spec's listed dispatch, release, and documentation areas; no unrelated behavior was added.

The standard Linux CLI uses the subtree shim and skips broad process matching. The no-shim fallback still treats a reviewer-settable environment value as ownership across all same-user PIDs; it can signal an unrelated run.

A run-scoped subreaper is the smallest sufficient Linux design after a dispatcher-wide subreaper proved too broad; a Windows job is the OS-native equivalent. Group kill alone misses session escapes, while a general process-management framework would add scope without value. The choice is invalidated where non-Linux paths do not wait/report (N2/N3), the Linux scan exceeds its bound (N4), or an embedder uses the settable-environment fallback (N1).

findings.action: Require the shim for untrusted reviewers or constrain fallback termination to verified run descendants; record a PID only after confirmed signal delivery and add a cross-run non-termination regression.
findings.rationale: The no-shim Linux fallback scans every same-user PID and accepts the reviewer-controlled POSE_SEALED_CHECKOUT value as ownership; pidfd pins a PID but does not prove run ancestry. A process from another run can set that value and be SIGKILLed. The fallback also records a candidate PID before confirming that a signal was delivered. The standard pose CLI enables the shim, but the fallback remains for embedders (spec L6).

findings.action: On non-Linux Unix, verifyReviewProcessGroup returns success without checking that the SIGKILLed process group is empty. Dispatch can proceed to cleanup inventory before a remaining group member has exited, contrary to R1's bounded wait. Poll for group disappearance within the bound and keep cleanup incomplete on timeout.

The run record lists ended PIDs only from reaped or shim-reported processes. Windows job termination and non-Linux Unix process-group termination leave reaped empty, so a run can terminate leftovers without recording which processes were ended, contrary to R2. Capture and persist the terminated process identities on those paths.

The five-second deadline is checked while reading /proc batches, but the subsequent loop reads stats and signals for every collected entry before checking the deadline at line 189; readProcBatched accumulates all entries. The no-shim Linux fallback has the same gap: reviewMarkedProcesses materializes /proc and reads every PID without a deadline (review_reap_linux.go:90-97). A large process table or reviewer process flood can make cleanup exceed its bound, contrary to R1. Stream entries through the per-process scans and check the deadline there.

recordReviewRun publishes the run witness before its transcript and JSON record. If releaseAbandonedAttemptClaimed is interrupted or a later publication fails in that gap, the witness makes ReadReviewRuns report incomplete history; the next release refuses in recordedAttemptRun (delegation_release.go:169-172) and leaves the stalled marker and reservation blocking future dispatch. Make this publication boundary recoverable and fault-test interruption before the run JSON is present.
